plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Rattlesnake AGI #1 Yoakum County, Texas
ama_definition: A half-mile buffer around the modeled plume at end of injection (2036), which also contains the 2041 plume, covering a 14-year monitoring period; a revised plan is due by 2036 (p42).
mma_definition: The stabilized plume after modeled density drift (about 2,177 acres) plus a buffer of at least half a mile (p41-42).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None are rated likely. Surface equipment and the AGI well (plus ten deep penetrations in the MMA) get most of the monitoring; faults, the confining layer and seismicity are rated unlikely or very low risk (p44-53).
baseline_summary: Operational baseline of injection volumes and pressures taken from SCADA, plus one pre-expansion groundwater sample from the operator's on-site water well analyzed by a third-party lab (p59-60).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 of the following year; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data. The appended TRRC permit requires monthly monitoring of injection pressure and volume reported annually on Form H-10 (p64, p67, p77).
notes: Plan is titled for the Rattlesnake AGI #1 well serving the 30-30 plant. The quarterly mobile CO2/H2S readings near penetrating wells, which the plan calls 'atmospheric monitoring', are coded under fixed_gas_detectors per the guide's scheduled-handheld-survey rule, not atmospheric_co2. Plan says MITs are annual; the appended TRRC permit only requires an annulus pressure test before injection and after workovers (p77). Seismic station frequency not stated. Monitoring runs for the 17-year injection period plus a proposed 5-year post-injection period (p56). Not EOR; no CO2 produced (p62).

plan_title: Brown Pelican CO2 Sequestration Project Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The modeled Area of Review (maximum pressure front at 12 years of injection combined with the CO2 plume 50 years after injection stops, about 5.4 square miles) plus a half-mile buffer (p16, p19).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the Area of Review plus a half-mile buffer (p19).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None. All eight pathways (legacy wells, project wells, faults, seismicity, surface equipment, confining zone, lateral migration, third-party drilling) are rated low likelihood and low magnitude given the mitigations; the three legacy wells in the AoR were re-plugged in February 2025 (p21-29).
baseline_summary: Roughly one year of pre-injection baseline: quarterly fluid and dissolved gas sampling in the Injection Zone and one USDW well, quarterly soil gas at 20 stations, injectate composition, pressure and temperature in 10 wells, site seismometers, quarterly DInSAR/GPS, and pre-injection VSP and 2D seismic on top of a 2022 3D survey (p20, p31, p43-44).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance; any confirmed leakage quantified case by case with a statistical error estimate; records kept at least three years. Monitoring is tied to the UIC Class VI permit's testing and monitoring plan and QASP. No commitment to publish measurement data (p35, p44-45, p49-50).
notes: Frequencies differ by period; rows give the injection-period frequency and detail notes the post-injection one. Inconsistencies: DInSAR after injection is 'annually for 10 years' in 7.1.7 (p34) but 'annual for five years or until plume stabilization' in Table 7 (p36); the USDW paragraph (p31) lists triggers for increasing 'soil gas sampling', apparently a drafting slip. Annual soil gas sampling from year 4 covers only a subset of the 20 stations, and after injection soil gas is event-driven only. The Confining Zone monitors sit in the Upper Confining Zone itself; the plan says no permeable zone lies between it and the USDW (p31). Atmospheric testing coded mentioned_only because it 'may be conducted' as a follow-up. Optical gas imaging coded under fixed_gas_detectors per the guide; no fixed sensors or personal monitors are described. Table 4 (p22) is interleaved with Table 5 in the text layer. Contents page says 'June 2025', cover says July 2025.

plan_title: MONITORING, REPORTING, AND VERIFICATION PLAN Bull Moose AGI #1 Targa Delaware, LLC (Targa)
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA; the regulatory AMA (end-of-injection plume in 2055 plus half a mile, and the 2060 plume) lies inside it (p47-49).
mma_definition: The stabilized plume at 2070 (1% saturation cutoff) plus a half-mile buffer; nearby faults lie outside, so no fault buffer was added (p48-49).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment, especially the well and its pipeline, is called a potential risk though very unlikely; drilling new wells through the injection zone could cause a surface release; three offset wells get a medium risk rating. Confining zone, lateral migration, faults and seismicity are very unlikely (p51-61).
baseline_summary: Planned 12 months of monthly groundwater sampling and soil CO2 flux measurements before moving to less frequent sampling, a seismic baseline from historical TexNet data, and H2S levels seen during inspections; DCS flags excursions in operating parameters (p67-70).
reporting_summary: Annual GHG reports and supporting records retained (period not stated). Targa says it will report data from its monitoring network and produce periodic seismic and groundwater chemistry reports, but names no recipient and makes no commitment to publish; TexNet data are public (p66, p68-69, p76).
notes: BM AGI #1 was permitted but not yet drilled (drilling planned Q4 2024), so in-well gauges and DTS are future commitments; the seismometer is described as already installed. Groundwater well count conflicts: p35 lists 2 domestic wells in the MMA, p55 says there are none, so sampling locations are unknown. Atmospheric monitoring is only named once (p67), so coded mentioned_only. No annulus monitoring is mentioned. Text cites a New Mexico rule (NMAC) for a Texas site (p51) and AGA Report #1 for orifice metering. Post-injection monitoring is 15 years (p5, p63).

plan_title: Amended Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan Campo Viejo Plant Pozo Acido Viejo No. 1 Esperanza No. 1 Yoakum County, Texas
ama_definition: Same boundary as the MMA, on the grounds that the only probable leakage paths are penetrating wells and surface equipment; it contains the plume through year 55 (p46).
mma_definition: The modeled plume 25 years after injection ends (about 3,337 acres, 1% gas saturation cutoff) plus a buffer of at least half a mile (p44-45).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wells penetrating the injection zone are rated 'possible' with medium magnitude (six offset penetrations); surface equipment is remote but monitored; drilling, faults, confining zone and seismicity are remote or very unlikely (p46-48).
baseline_summary: Injection volume and pressure measurements taken before the original 2022 plan was implemented, plus a 2022 baseline sample from the on-site water well; 2023 and 2024 samples reported no variance (p68-69).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 of the following year; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data or to report monitoring results to the state is stated in the plan text (p73, p76).
notes: Amendment adds Esperanza No. 1 (permit pending at time of writing) and replaces Estacado No. 1, now shut in. Appendix pages with the step-rate test and the Pozo Acido Viejo UIC order/GAU letter are image-only (p81-85, p91-95), so permit monitoring conditions could not be checked. Personal H2S monitors listed 'As needed' in Table 11; frequency coded unspecified. Quarterly handheld CO2 'atmospheric monitoring' near penetrations coded under fixed_gas_detectors, not atmospheric_co2. 'Regional seismic evaluation' (p47) may refer to reflection seismic or seismicity review; unclear.

plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Copperhead AGI #001, Targa Midstream Services, LLC (Targa)
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA; the plume at the end of 30 years of injection (2055) plus a half-mile buffer, enlarged to take in the nearby fault trace, falls inside the MMA (p43).
mma_definition: The stabilized plume (no growth after 2060) plus a half-mile buffer, joined with the trace of the northern fault (Fault 1) plus a half-mile buffer (p40-42).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None rated more than very unlikely or low. Surface equipment (injection well, TAG pipeline, flanges, relief valves) is called the most likely source; the plugged Woolley #001 inside the plume is the only well rated low risk (p45-47, p51-54).
baseline_summary: DCS operating set points and the H2S contingency plan, plus planned pre-injection baselines: 12 months of monthly groundwater sampling and soil CO2 flux, and historical regional seismicity from the New Mexico Tech network (p61-64).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance. The plan also mentions a periodic seismic report with an event map and a groundwater chemistry report, with no stated recipient. No commitment to publish or share measurement data (p62-63, p67, p70).
notes: Well not yet drilled (planned 2025); plan says it will be re-evaluated after drilling (p67, p70). Groundwater monitoring is committed, but the plan also says there are no active groundwater wells in the MMA (p46); sampling locations are never identified. Red Hills wells 5+ miles away are cited as Targa sampling (p30). The 'CO2 monitoring network' (p62) is undefined; Table 6-1 calls it a LiCor flux network, so atmospheric_co2 coded mentioned_only and the LiCor work coded as soil_gas. DTS fiber coded under cased_hole_logging. MIT interval not stated. Text cites a Figure 5.6-2 that does not exist and refers to Texas (p6, p70) although the site is in New Mexico.

plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Independence AGI #1 and #2 Wells, Pinon Midstream, LLC
ama_definition: Same as the MMA; because the plume is not stable by t+5, the AMA uses the largest plume extent of any modeled scenario (through about year 50) plus a half-mile buffer (p47-48).
mma_definition: The maximum extent of any modeled plume in any scenario at any time (stabilizing around year 50) plus a half-mile buffer (p47-48).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: All pathways rated low or unlikely. The plan singles out the West Jal B Deep #001 brine injection well, which penetrates the injection zone about a mile away, as possible but unlikely; the plume reaches mapped faults but leakage is called unlikely (p49-53).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is the H2S contingency plan monitoring (daily inspections, fixed and personal H2S monitors) and DCS operating set points (p57-58).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance, under an internal Greenhouse Gas Monitoring Plan. The onsite seismic station sends data to the New Mexico Tech Seismic Network as required by the NMOCC order. No commitment to publish measurement data (p23, p53, p58, p62-64).
notes: Pages 21, 65 and 86-100 are image-only or blank (86-100 hold Appendix 9 West Jal Unit #1 plugging records and Appendix 10 flow diagram). Mobile CO2 surveys coded as atmospheric_co2, not fixed_gas_detectors. The fault surveys have no stated schedule. No groundwater sampling, even though 15 water wells lie within 2 miles (p29). Text calls the injection meters both volumetric and Coriolis (p60, p62). Says implementation on June 1, 2023, although this is version 5.0, February 2024 (p61).

plan_title: CapturePoint LLC Denver City Field Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The George Allen Unit and Ruth Hudson Lease boundaries plus a half-mile buffer; the plume is projected to stay inside the unit boundaries through 2037 and for five years after injection (p19, p21).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA, because the projected plume is smaller than the unit area (p19-20).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores and surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated low risk (p22-27).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data (injection rates and pressures, production forecasts, visual inspections, H2S alarms) used to flag excursions (p33-34).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed with other GHGRP reports by March 31, with the mass balance and estimated leakage; simple leak repairs also go in the Subpart W report; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data or report to the state UIC program (p27, p31, p39, p42).
notes: Close to the Wellman plan (same operator, same template), with two differences: it adds permanent ground-level H2S monitors throughout the field (coded fixed_gas_detectors) and it has no radioactive tracer survey. MIT appears only in the response-plan table with no interval or rule citation; coded committed because it is listed as monitoring, but it is thin. The plan says CapturePoint 'monitors the USGS earthquake monitoring ... site' (p25); coded passive_seismic committed (public network only, no site instruments). Wellman has the same sentence (its p22) and was coded mentioned_only, so one of the two should be harmonized. Section 5.8 says injection pressure (not reservoir pressure, as in Wellman) is continuously monitored. The CO2 supply pipeline is called Kinder Morgan in some places and Trinity in others (p14, p29, p35). Figures are images.

plan_title: Oxy Wasson San Andres Field Amended Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The combined boundary of the Denver, Willard, Wasson ODC and Bennett Ranch units plus a half-mile buffer (p21).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the four unit boundaries plus a half-mile buffer, since the stabilized plume is expected to stay inside the field (p22).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores and surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, third-party drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated negligible or low (p23-28).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline (CO2 flooding began in 1983). The baseline is existing automated operational data (injection set points and flags, production forecasts, inspection work orders, H2S alarms) used to flag excursions (p35-36).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report, filed around March 31 with other GHG reports, with the mass balance and estimated leakage; well changes noted in the annual report; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data (p5, p28, p35-36, p40, p42-43).
notes: The file for this slug is Oxy's July 2023 amended Wasson San Andres Field plan, which folds the Denver Unit's December 2015 plan into one plan covering the Denver, Willard, Wasson ODC and Bennett Ranch units. Production tests run about every two months; coded periodic_unspecified because the vocabulary has no bimonthly value. Table 2 lists five 'MON TEMP' monitoring wells, none active (4 plugged, 1 temporarily abandoned), and the plan gives them no monitoring role (p14). The plan says H2S in the injected gas is below the analyzer's detection threshold (p35), which limits the H2S-as-proxy approach; unlike the CapturePoint plans, no permanent H2S detectors are described. Reservoir pressure is said to be measured but no instruments or wells are named. Figures and maps are images. Pages 46-160 are the well list.

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Libby AGI No. 1 and Libby AGI No. 2, Lea County, New Mexico
ama_definition: By rule the end-of-injection (year 20) plume plus a half-mile buffer combined with the year 25 plume, but because the difference is small the operator set the AMA equal to the MMA (p59).
mma_definition: The modeled stabilized plume (about 651 acres, 50 years after injection stops) plus a half-mile buffer (p59).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None rated above low. Surface equipment (pipeline flanges, valves, wellheads) is described as the most likely failure point during injection; three wells penetrate the injection zone in the MMA, one plugged well inside the stabilized plume (p61-66).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection soil gas sampling near selected well locations in the MMA (scheduled Q4 2025, third-party lab), ambient H2S and CO2 levels set during amine unit commissioning, and initial reservoir pressure measurements; after that, SCADA operational data serve as the baseline (p75-78, p84).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 through e-GGRT (draft in Appendix D); injected volumes and pressures also reported to NMOCD under Class II rules; records kept at least three years; amended plan with an updated plume due before the end of year 5. No commitment to publish measurement data (p84, p86-87).
notes: Pre-construction plan: wells scheduled to be built Q1 2026 and operating Q2 2026 (p3), yet p82 says injection begins Q3 2025. Acid gas is about 80% CO2 / 20% H2S, so H2S detection is the main CO2 proxy and the plan rules out direct leak surveys for safety (p78, p81). Fixed detector set points conflict: Table 6 gives 10 ppm alarm / 90 ppm shutdown (p65), text says 'setpoints at 10 ppm and alarm at 15 ppm' (p75). The seismic section calls NM03 a TexNet station and cites a nonexistent Figure 42 (p77). Soil gas location count is not stated. Atmospheric CO2 coded mentioned_only because only a one-time commissioning baseline is described. Figures and Appendices A-D (plot plan, well table, draft report) are images or not in the text. Printed page numbers are one less than PDF page numbers used here.

plan_title: Oxy Hobbs Field CO2 Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The Hobbs Field boundary (North and South Hobbs Units), on the grounds that CO2 is already present throughout the field and kept there by fluid management; no buffer is added (p30-31).
mma_definition: The Hobbs Field plus a half-mile buffer (p31).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wellbores (about 700 field wells plus offset wells) and surface equipment are the pathways Oxy manages; faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, new drilling and diffuse seal leakage are judged minimal or very unlikely (p4, p32-38).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The 'baselines' are the existing automated data systems: injection set points from pattern modeling, production forecasts, visual inspection work orders and H2S alarms, screened for possible CO2 leakage (p44-45).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed with other GHG reports by March 31, giving the mass balance and leak estimates; records kept at least three years. Well leaks are also reported to NMOCD and surface-facility leaks under Subpart W. No commitment to publish measurement data (p37-38, p45, p50, p52-53).
notes: Well-test frequency is inconsistent: about every two months (p24, p33) but 'once during each monthly cycle' on p41; coded periodic_unspecified. 'Reservoir pressure' is read at WAG headers and in new wells (Table 3, p37-38); no observation wells or bottom-hole gauges are named. Fixed H2S sensors exist only where the voluntary SFRM program applies; coverage not stated. The 'two-part' visual inspection never clearly defines the second part. AMA has no buffer; the MMA adds the half mile. Older-style plan (2017): no seismic, soil gas, groundwater or atmospheric monitoring.

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan, Kinder Morgan Permian CCS LLC
ama_definition: Same as the MMA: a 9,500 ft radius around the KSU 2361 well, built from the plume at stabilization (30 years after injection ends) and at t+5 plus a half-mile buffer (p57-58).
mma_definition: A circle of 9,500 ft radius around KSU 2361: the modeled stabilized plume radius of 6,850 ft plus a half-mile buffer (p57-58).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None. Surface equipment, the single injection wellbore (the only well reaching the injection interval in the MMA), faults, the confining layer and seismicity are all rated unlikely; surface equipment and the injection well get the most monitoring (p59-67).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines: 12 months of ambient CO2 to set fixed-monitor alarm levels, atmospheric and topsoil CO2 at the well site and within the MMA, and groundwater samples from new monitoring wells; injection volumes and pressures baselined at startup (p59, 69-70, 74-75).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 with the mass balance; records kept at least three years; plan revised within 180 days of material changes. No commitment to publish or share monitoring data and no stated reporting of results to the TRRC (p79, 81-82).
notes: Every page carries an 'EXEMPT - FOIA ... CRITICAL ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE INFORMATION - DO NOT RELEASE' stamp, though the plan was obtained as a public filing. Appendices A-D (including Appendix C on safety systems) have no text in the file (p85). Table 10's text extraction scrambles which method goes with which pathway; rows were coded from the section text. Soil gas is called 'proposed' in Section 5.3, but Section 6.2 firmly commits to baseline topsoil measurements, so it is coded committed. Quarterly atmospheric monitoring is tied to penetrating wells and none exist, so in practice it covers the AGI well site. The AMA is given as 3,384 acres, which is the plume area, not the 9,500 ft circle. Monitoring runs for injection plus a 'proposed' 5-year post-injection period, though the plume is modeled to stabilize 30 years after injection. No bottom-hole or reservoir pressure monitoring is described. Coded acid_gas_disposal because the plan frames the well as a treated acid gas (AGI) well, although the expected stream is 99.2% CO2 with no H2S. Every page of the posted plan carries a "Critical Energy Infrastructure Information - DO NOT RELEASE" stamp. EPA posts the plan publicly, but out of caution this dataset cites pages for this site and does not quote it.

plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Frontier Field Services, LLC (Frontier) Acid Gas Injection Facility, Metropolis, Maljamar AGI #1 and Maljamar AGI #2 Wells
ama_definition: Equal to the MMA in both parts: Part A the Metropolis plume at 2053 and 2058 plus a half mile; Part B the superposed AGI #1 and #2 plumes at end of injection (2043, 2046) and five years later plus a half mile (p53, p137-138).
mma_definition: Part A: modeled Metropolis acid gas plume at end of injection (2053) plus a half-mile buffer; Part B: superposed plumes of Maljamar AGI #1 (2043) and AGI #2 (2046) plus a half-mile buffer (p52-53, p137).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: In both parts, surface equipment (injection wells, pipelines, flanges, relief valves) is the likely pathway and the injection wells themselves possible but unlikely; other wells, water wells, the seal, lateral migration, faults and seismicity are rated unlikely to highly unlikely using NRAP and a 5x5 risk matrix (p55-65, p140-152).
baseline_summary: Both parts: past injection volume and CO2 concentration history (Maljamar has years of Subpart UU data) and DCS set points; plus new baselines of six monthly groundwater and soil flux rounds before going quarterly, and historical seismic records (p72-74, p77, p161-163, p166).
reporting_summary: One combined annual Subpart RR report for both plants under a single GHGRP ID, with narratives of monitoring efforts and anomalies; pipeline leaks reported to NMOCD; NMBGMR seismic analysis to be made public. No commitment to publish other monitoring data (p3-7, p56, p73, p141, p162).
notes: One plan in two parts: Part A (Dagger Draw plant, Metropolis well, PDF p15-97) and Part B (Maljamar plant, AGI #1 and #2, p98-198). Monitoring text is nearly identical; differences are flagged in rows. Conflicts: MIT annual (6.2) vs order's two-year casing test (Part A p59); personal H2S alarm 10 ppm (quoted contingency plans) vs 5 ppm (Section 7.2); Part A maximum wellhead pressure 3,280 psi (p59) vs 1,980 psi (p63); Section 7.6 cites state seismometers within 10 miles but the nearest named stations are 15 mi (A) and 11.8 mi (B). Groundwater wells 'will be identified'. Bottom-hole gauge appears only in 6.2. Monitoring stated for duration of injection only (p67, p154). Part B 2.1 gives an ID 'for Daggers Draw' (likely typo). Dagger Draw spectrometer expected operational Sept 2023 (p77). Cover, figures and appendices (p175-198) are image-only.

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan for the Delaware CCS Hub Facility
uic_class_per_plan: VI and II (Delaware CCS #1, #2 and #5 Class VI; Loving AGI #3 and #4 Class II)
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: the end-of-injection (2038) plume plus a half-mile buffer superimposed on the 2043 plume (p26).
mma_definition: Three separate MMAs around the facilities' plumes: the modeled CO2 extent 50 years after injection ends, plus a half-mile buffer, totaling about 38.9 square miles; MMA #3 (CCS #5) not yet modeled (p24-25).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None. Surface equipment and injection wells are rated low likelihood; existing and future wells, groundwater wells, faults, the confining system and seismicity are rated extremely low. None of the 758 wells in the MMAs reaches the seal (p27-35).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection environmental baseline: ambient and near-surface CO2 (including vadose-zone soil gas), fluid samples from the Pecos Valley and Rustler aquifers, the first permeable zone above the injection interval and the injection interval, pre-injection pulsed-neutron and cased-hole logs, and baseline CSEM and microseismic surveys (p39, 41).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31; testing and monitoring plan reviewed at least every five years; records kept at least three years. Seismic events over M2.5 within 10 km 'will be reported' (recipient unstated). No commitment to publish measurement data (p35, 44-45).
notes: Hub of five wells: three Class VI and two Class II AGI wells, all with UIC numbers 'Not Yet Assigned'; coded class_vi_storage because most of the planned volume goes to the Class VI wells. Soil gas, groundwater and above-zone fluid sampling are described only as pre-injection baselines; they are coded committed with frequency one_time, and no repeat schedule is given. Internal inconsistencies: Table 7 gives cement bond logs a 5-year interval while the text says 'as-needed'; Table 7 lists the pulsed-neutron log as both 'As Needed' and '5 Year Interval'; p35 says six seismometers around the Central Loving Facility, with stations at MMA #2/#3 only 'likely', while p40 says six per MMA. In-zone monitoring wells are referenced but never specified. Airborne CO2 sensors (atmospheric_co2) and the hub gas detectors (fixed_gas_detectors) may be the same equipment. Details are deferred to the Class VI permit's testing and monitoring plan, which is not included. The last page carries a Milestone notice calling the document confidential and proprietary. Soil gas recoded to mentioned_only after the independent check: the only support is an example in the baseline sentence (p41).

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Mongoose AGI No. 1 Mitchell County, TX
ama_definition: A half-mile buffer around the modeled plume after 12 years of injection (2036), which also contains the 2041 plume; covers a 12-year period, with a revised plan due by 2036 (p66).
mma_definition: The plume after 40 years of injection plus 120 years of density drift (about 3,280 acres, 3% saturation cutoff) plus a half-mile buffer (p65-66).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface equipment is rated 'possible' (during injection); existing wells (two plugged penetrations), faults, the confining layer and seismicity are all rated unlikely with low magnitude (p68).
baseline_summary: Pre-implementation soil gas sampling at the AGI well and one plugged penetration (to be completed by May 20, 2024), atmospheric H2S at the well, a baseline atmospheric CO2 concentration at plant commissioning, and injection volume/pressure baselines once injection starts (p72, p79-80, p83).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 of the following year, and annual soil gas results are to be included in it (the p72 wording says only if they indicate an issue); records kept at least three years. No other commitment to publish data (p72, p80, p88, p91).
notes: Appendices A-D (TRRC permit, operating safety plan, site plan, well list) are listed but not in the text file, so permit conditions and detector locations could not be checked. Groundwater conflicts: Table 13 lists annual groundwater samples, but the text says none of the three database wells exist; coded mentioned_only. Producer gas analysis coded as above_zone_monitoring, not production_monitoring (not EOR). No personal H2S monitors mentioned. The 120-year post-injection monitoring period (p78) is unusually long. Some geology pages are image-only or garbled; the monitoring sections read cleanly.

plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Red Hills AGI #1 and Red Hills AGI #3, Targa Northern Delaware, LLC (TND)
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: it covers the modeled plume at end of injection (2054) and five years later (2059), plus a half-mile buffer (p40).
mma_definition: The stabilized modeled acid gas plume at 2059 plus a half-mile buffer (p40).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment (injection wells, the line to them, flanges, relief valves) is the most likely pathway; lateral migration along channel sands is rated possible; existing and groundwater wells possible-to-improbable with minimal magnitude; seal, faults and seismicity improbable per NRAP modeling (p41-46).
baseline_summary: DCS operating data and H2S Contingency Plan monitoring, plus purpose-built baselines: 12 months of monthly groundwater and soil CO2 flux sampling, and historical seismic records (p53-55). Plan says baseline monitoring has been under way for several years (p59).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR reporting through GHG reports and records retention; pipeline leaks reported to NMOCD; NMBGMR seismic analysis and maps to be made publicly available; a groundwater chemistry report to be prepared; TND to take over monitoring, recording and reporting of the New Mexico Tech network data. No commitment to publish other measurement data (p52-54, p61-62).
notes: PDF page 1 is a cover notice only; figure pages (detector map p28, monitoring network map p56) and appendix records (p87-92) are image-only. Groundwater, soil flux and atmospheric work are run by New Mexico Tech under a DOE grant, with TND to take over. DTS coded as cased_hole_logging though it is permanent fiber. MIT interval not stated. No production at site (p58), so production_monitoring is not_found. Monitoring covers injection plus a 5-year post-injection period (p47). Atmospheric sampling is coded committed (periodic, unspecified) to match Wildcat, whose plan uses the same language (p52-53), although no instruments, locations or frequency are given and the Figure 7-1 network map shows none.

plan_title: CapturePoint LLC Seminole East Field Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The East Seminole San Andres Unit and Lindoss Unit boundaries; the projected CO2 storage area (about 1,000 acres) sits inside the 2,045-acre field outline (p16).

plan_title: Blue Spruce Operating LLC Dry Piney "Jackalope" Gas Processing Facility & Dry Piney State Acid Gas Injection Wells Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Plan

ama_definition: BSO sets the AMA equal to the MMA by choosing t = 2128 (end of a 50-year injection period plus 50-year stabilization), so the plume-plus-buffer area including the fault pathways coincides with the MMA polygon (p48-49).

The plugged Tip Top T62X-16S, the only non-BSO well penetrating the injection zone, is rated 'unlikely' (p54-59). Figures are image-only (e.g., p10, 12, 14-17, 24-25, 29-33, 35-40, 43-48, 50, 53-54, 56, 62, 65-66, 68, 72); Appendix B wellbore diagram (p119) has no text; Appendix D (p122-130) is OCR of scanned lab reports; bold/italic marking of baseline candidate wells in Appendices A and C is lost in extraction. (2) Satellite hyperspectral/Lidar imaging appears in Table 5.1 and has a stated schedule in 6.3 (semiannual two years, then annual), but every narrative mention says BSO is 'investigating' its use and 'would' employ it, so it is coded mentioned_only; this is the weakest supportable level, and it could be read as committed. (4) In-well gauges and DTS/DAS are described only for the Dry Piney State 12-16 (Section 5.3.1), though Table 5.1 lists in-well pressure/temperature sensors for all AGI wells. Plan states monitoring continues through injection and the 50-year post-injection period (p74). Plan itself notes it would assume 1-3 months (up to ~1.25 Mt) to detect leakage via shallow wells and 12-18 months (4.5-6.75 Mt) via surface methods (p78-82). plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Lima Tango CCS 1

baseline_summary: Three parts: (1) pre-injection groundwater quality from a monitoring well, but only if a freshwater aquifer is found when logging the injection well (quarterly sampling the first year, then possibly annual); (2) a seismicity baseline from TexNet/USGS historical data starting in 2019; (3) operational performance baselines built from continuous injection pressure, temperature, rate and annulus pressure/temperature data once injection begins in 2026 (p49).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equation RR-12; no CO2 produced). Any leakage estimates and the methods used are to be reported in the annual monitoring report; surface-equipment leaks quantified under Subpart W are 'included in recurring reporting'; MRV plan to be updated if new wells are drilled in the MMA. Records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish or share measurement data or to report monitoring results to the TRRC beyond the permit (p40, p45-47, p51, p55).
notes: Pre-operational plan: the well had not been drilled (drilling planned Q3 2025, injection early 2026). Page 60 (Appendix 13.3, W-1/W-14 permits) has no text; pages 35, 37 and 41 contain garbled figure characters. AVO inspection frequency is stated inconsistently: monthly (p40), daily inspections plus monthly AVO (p44), and 'daily to weekly AVO inspections' (p49); coded as monthly with detail noting the others. The only reservoir-pressure measurement is the bottomhole gauge in the injection well itself; there are no observation wells. Groundwater monitoring is explicitly conditional on finding a freshwater response in open-hole logs of the injector (the plan notes no water wells within two miles), so the groundwater baseline exists only in that case. Open-hole logs over each casing interval during drilling (p47) are site characterization, not cased-hole monitoring, so cased_hole_logging is not_found. Section 6.7 lists many quantification technologies (atmospheric sensing, UAV, eddy covariance, open-path lasers, NDIR, soil flux, reservoir models) only as options to be 'considered' if a leak is detected; these are coded mentioned_only. The static/dynamic model is to be updated with core and log data after drilling (p28). Monitoring period stated as the 12-year injection period plus a proposed two-year post-injection period (p44). Risk ranking uses the CARB CCS Protocol likelihood matrix (p38-39).

plan_title: Lisbon Valley, Utah Gas Processing Plant Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan
ama_definition: The half-mile buffer around the modeled free-phase CO2 plume at year 2060 (30 years of injection plus 10 years post-injection), drawn so it also contains the plume projected for 2065 (p37-38).
mma_definition: The combined P10/P50/P90 modeled plume footprint at year 2205 (150 years post-injection, when the plume stabilizes against the graben fault) plus a half-mile buffer; monitoring is proposed to end in 2205 (p35-36, p38).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None is treated as likely. Surface equipment (flanges and valves on the acid-gas pipeline and plant) is the only pathway given more than negligible likelihood, and even that is rated low (p39). Legacy wells, faults and seal leakage were modeled with NRAP-Open-IAM as zero risk; future drilling, lateral migration and induced seismicity are called negligible or highly unlikely (p39-53).
baseline_summary: A mix: DCS target ranges and trigger thresholds for injection rate, pressure and composition (operational baseline); plus described pre-injection baselines for a suite of MITs on the injector, ambient H2S checks, documented baseline inspections, at least four seasonal rounds of soil CO2 flux at an array of collars (thresholds set at a high percentile), and temperature/pressure/fluid composition at one selected USDW water well (p56-57). Note that injection has been ongoing since 2015, so 'prior to injection' baselines can only be pre-plan or pre-rate-increase.
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report using equations RR-1 to RR-12 (received, injected, surface leakage, sequestered), with surface equipment leaks estimated per Subpart W; quarterly records of received and injected CO2 and annual records of leakage calculations retained under 40 CFR 98.3(g) (p57-64). Annual MIT on the injector under 40 CFR 146.8 (p54). No commitment to publish or share measurement data; no explicit commitment to report monitoring results to the state UIC program, though the plan relies on DOGM/EPA oversight of drilling (p40).
notes: No version number or date is printed; the plan says it takes effect in Q2/Q3 2025 after EPA approval (p62). Prepared by the University of Utah EGI/CSI for GNG Energy. Injection has been ongoing since 2015 (June 1 on p28, July 1 on p62), so section 6 baselines described as 'prior to injection' (MIT suite, inspections, soil flux, USDW well) are ambiguous in timing; coded baseline=yes because the plan describes them as pre-monitoring reference measurements. Personal H2S alarm threshold is given as 10 ppm on p39 and ~5 ppm on p54. Soil flux duration is ambiguous: p55 says seasonal monitoring 'for 5 years following the injection period' while p56-57 refers to flux values collected during and after injection; 5 years post-injection is far shorter than the 150-year monitoring timeframe (p38, p62). reservoir_pressure coded committed on the strength of p46-47 language about pressure and fluid monitoring at the injection well, but this may simply be the DCS wellhead data; no gauges or observation wells are named. The seismic station is only 'suggested' (p53). Section 7.3 states no production, yet section 9.1 contains template text on quarterly sampling of produced gas and a recycle compressor meter, and p48 refers to 'Targa' (apparently copied from another plan). Several figure pages (e.g. p22-24, p26-27, p31-34) are image-only apart from captions; Tables 4 and 5 and the stratigraphic chart on p9 are garbled in extraction but not needed for coding. No annulus pressure, above-zone, logging, deformation or atmospheric CO2 monitoring is described.

plan_title: North Burbank Unit (NBU) CO2 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The AMA is the North Burbank Unit boundary itself, because injected CO2 is held within the unit by structure and water-curtain injection; it expands as CO2-EOR moves into other parts of the unit (p20-21).
mma_definition: The MMA is the NBU unit boundary plus the required half-mile buffer, since the free-phase plume is expected to stay within the unit (p21).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only wellbores (about 2,845 wells, roughly 2,394 inactive or abandoned) and pipelines/surface equipment are treated as realistic pathways; faults/fractures, natural and induced seismicity, prior operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated improbable or very low (p4, p22-29).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data: daily field monitoring, SCADA data, target injection rates/pressures, production forecasts, routine inspections, H2S alarms, plant/pipeline set points and MITs, used to flag excursions from expected performance (p34-36).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed with other GHG reports by March 31, containing the mass balance (RR-2 through RR-11, using RCF outlet and satellite/RCF inlet meters rather than per-well meters) and any quantified leakage events; AMA expansions and facility changes are described in the annual report; event records kept at least 3 years. No commitment to publish measurement data or to report monitoring results to the UIC program beyond permit requirements (p21, p34, p36-42).
notes: No image-only pages; figures and the well list (p56-91) carry little monitoring text. Well-test frequency is inconsistent: p23 says each producer is tested about every two months, p31 says once every quarter; quarterly is coded (weaker). MIT is 'periodic (and in many instances an annual)', so coded periodic_unspecified rather than annual. 'Continual, automated pressure monitoring in the injection zone' (p31) cross-references Section 4.1, which describes injection-well pressure, so reservoir_pressure is coded mentioned_only despite several references to reservoir pressure. 'Gas alarms' (p29) appear only in a list with no description. Seismic networks are cited for risk characterization only. Section 7.4 refers to quantification approaches 'in Section 5.1', apparently meaning 5.8. The plan acknowledges a prior operator let small amounts of CO2 move past the western unit boundary (p20, p27-28); response would be quantification and reporting, not added subsurface monitoring. Mass balance uses aggregated RCF/satellite meters because of per-well meter error (p37, p38).

plan_title: Purdy-Bradley Springer Field: Northeast Purdy Springer Unit (NEPSU) / South East Bradley A Unit (SEBAU) Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The combined NEPSU and SEBAU unit boundaries plus a buffer of at least one-half mile, where the free-phase CO2 is expected to stay through 2054 and five years after (p34).
mma_definition: Defined as identical to the AMA: the two unit boundaries plus a half-mile buffer, since the plume is expected to be held by the reservoir's geologic truncation limits (p6, p34-35).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores (especially legacy wells and drilling of new wells) and surface equipment are treated as the realistic pathways ('unlikely but possible'); shallow groundwater wells, faults/fractures, lateral movement, the confining seal and seismicity are all rated unlikely with low magnitude (p5, p36-39, p41, p46).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data on injection well pressures and rates plus pattern performance; the plan may elect to collect ambient air data later. Reference gas values cited: 0.6% CO2 in the Cunningham before 1982 injection, 0.25% average in Hart wells sampled October 2023, and basin-wide published CO2 ranges, to be consulted if a leak is detected (p39, p46).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equation RR-11) and any leakage events with estimated amounts; records kept at least three years; mechanical failures of surface casing or cement reported to the appropriate regulatory authority. No commitment to publish measurement data (p42, p45, p47, p50, p53).
notes: Figure pages (p10-12, 14-15, 17-19, 23-25, 27-29, 32-33, 37, 40) carry only captions; Figure 22 well map and the Appendix 1 well list (886 wellbores) are not in the text. Groundwater is contradictory: p36 commits to annual testing of one groundwater well, while p46 says USDW wells have not been monitored; coded as committed on the explicit 'will test' sentence. MIT frequency is annual or five-yearly depending on permitted rate, so coded multi_year. Reservoir pressure is listed as a monitoring provision, yet p30 says actual reservoir pressure was unavailable and the last measurement dates to Fox et al. (1988); hence mentioned_only. Visual inspection frequency is stated as 'weekly or daily' (p42), daily for surface equipment (p46), weekly in Table 4; coded weekly as the floor. Soil gas and RTS use permissive 'may elect'/'sometimes' language. No fresh CO2 has been received since 2022; implementation is expected in 2026 after approval and securing a new CO2 supply (p13, p50). No seismic surveys, personal or fixed gas detectors, InSAR or microseismic arrays are mentioned.

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan O'Neal Gas Unit Well No. 4
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: the circular area around the single injector covering the modeled stabilized plume plus a half-mile buffer, after checking that the plume five years past end of injection stays inside the 12-year plume plus buffer; a revised AMA/MMA is promised by 2037 (p48, p50).
mma_definition: A circle around the O'Neal No. 4 covering the modeled free-phase plume after 12 years of injection and 10 years of density drift (about 0.45 mi radius, 303 acres) plus a half-mile all-around buffer (p48).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated low magnitude. Surface equipment is the only one rated 'possible' (during injection); existing wells (one plugged well penetrates the injection zone), faults (nearest interpreted fault about 4.25 mi away), the Pearsall confining zone, and natural/induced seismicity are all 'unlikely', with any vertical migration expected to be caught in a shallower gas reservoir (p52, p55, p61-62).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines are planned: baseline readings of the fixed H2S/CO2 monitors during commissioning, an atmospheric CO2 concentration at the facility, soil gas samples near the one plugged penetrating well, and groundwater samples from water wells (pH, TDS, CO2, VOC), all estimated for Oct. 1, 2024 but tied to permit/EPA approval. Operational baseline of injection volumes and pressures is recorded at start of injection (p65, p72-73, p77).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed March 31 with the RR-12 mass balance; soil gas and groundwater lab results are included in the annual report only if they show a material variance from baseline; flare/blowdown emissions are reported under the facility's GHG reporting and Subpart W; records kept at least 3 years. No commitment to publish measurement data; MRV plan revisions to EPA within 180 days (p72-73, p75-77, p79-80).
notes: Class II permit was pending at submission; the plan says baseline data cannot be dated until the permit issues and the MRV plan will be implemented on EPA approval (p77). Figure-only pages (49, 51, 56-58, 60, 63, 66, 69, 71) and the appendices (81-82 are index pages only; forms, well lists not included). Annulus pressure is coded committed on a single sentence that implies monitoring without describing it (p67). Above-zone monitoring uses third-party-style producing gas wells; composition sampling frequency is not stated beyond 'regular' and 'monthly production statements', and whether Ozona operates these wells is not said. production_monitoring is not_found because this is not EOR (no CO2 produced, p75); the produced-gas CO2 checks are coded under above_zone_monitoring. Atmospheric CO2 is coded mentioned_only because only a one-time pre-operation baseline is promised and it may simply be the commissioning baseline of the fixed H2S/CO2 monitors (Table 10). Groundwater sampling: baseline on all wells but 'select wells' annually (p73). Minor inconsistencies: stabilized plume year given as 2047 (p16, p61) and 2062 (p26); TexNet station figure referenced as Figure 38 but is Figure 39 (p70-71). Monitoring commitment covers 12-year injection plus a 10-year post-injection period (p64).

plan_title: Petra Nova West Ranch Oil Field CO2 Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The existing West Ranch 41-A/98-A (Consolidated) Unit boundary plus a half-mile buffer, to be expanded to cover any new unit formed for CO2 EOR within the Project Interval, plus the same buffer (p24-25).
mma_definition: The outermost boundary of all Frio reservoirs in the Project Interval that could be developed by CO2 EOR, set by oil-water contacts and structure, plus a half-mile buffer (p25-26).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated low or highly unlikely. The plan invests most in legacy wellbores (389 P&A, 277 shut-in) and surface equipment; diffuse seal leakage, faults, seismicity, new wells, future drilling and lateral migration are dismissed on geologic grounds (p27-31).
baseline_summary: Operational data: daily field rounds, SCADA pressure data from injection, production and shut-in wells, and routine testing/maintenance, with 10% pressure deviations flagged (p35-36). A DOE MVA Plan collected a pre-flood baseline a year before injection, but this plan does not describe those measurements (p4); baseline RST logs were run on six wells (p29).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report (filed by March 31) with the mass balance, surface leakage estimates and well status changes; Subpart W reporting continues; records kept at least three years; TRRC annual injection report and H-5 MIT forms filed with the state. No commitment to publish measurement data (p20, p23, p36, p41-43).
notes: Figures (p8-13, 16-17, 19, 21, 26, 32, 35, 38) are images with little text; the inactive-well location map (p32) is image-only. MIT frequency is stated two ways: annual Casing Integrity Tests under TAC 16 §5.305(1)(C) (p23) and H-5 MITs at least every five years (p36); coded as multi_year with both noted. The pre-injection DOE MVA Plan baseline is referenced (p4) but none of its measurements (e.g., soil gas or groundwater) are described or carried into this plan, so those methods are coded not_found. The p31 statement that alarms notify 'if there are any CO2 releases from the subsurface' appears to refer to pressure alarms, not gas sensors. Corrosion monitoring requirement is said to be met by SCADA monitoring (p23). Reservoir_pressure and above_zone_monitoring both draw on the same 255-well shut-in pressure program (Table 5.1.1, p33), split by whether the zone is the injection reservoir.

plan_title: Scout Energy Management, LLC Rangely Field Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The boundary of the Rangely Field (Rangely Weber Sand Unit) plus a one-half mile buffer, since free-phase CO2 is already present throughout the field and is retained by pressure and lease-line fluid management (p19-20).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the Rangely Field Unit boundary plus the required one-half mile buffer, because the plume is expected to stay within the unit (p20).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wellbores and pipeline/surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults/fractures, natural and induced seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated very low risk (p21-26).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data captured by existing automatic data systems: visual inspection work orders, personal H2S monitor alarms, SCADA injection rate/pressure set points, and production volume/composition forecasts used to flag excursions (p30-31).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report (filed by March 31) with the mass balance and estimated surface leakage; records retained at least three years; well failures and MIT results reported in parallel to COGCC and equipment leaks under Subpart W. No commitment to publish measurement data (p25-26, p29, p35-37).
notes: No image-only pages; figures are referenced but their content is not in the text. Appendix 5 (p43-67) is a well list in which 'Monitor' status means a well used for bottom-hole reservoir pressure; these are the monitor wells referenced in Table 3 but the plan never states their number or survey instruments. Reservoir pressure surveys are '1 to 2 times per year'; coded as annual (the weaker reading). Production well tests are 'twice per month'; coded as monthly with the actual cadence in detail. Table 3 lists 'high pressure found in new wells' as a monitoring method although SEM has drilled no new wells. The plan cites a Section 2.2.3 and Figures 11/12 that do not exist. 'Pressure transducers with low pressure alarms' on surface equipment (p24) are pressure sensors, not gas detectors, so fixed_gas_detectors is not_found. The response table lists 'Loss of bottom-hole pressure control' with 'blowout during well operations' as the monitoring entry, which is not a monitoring method.

plan_title: Red Trail Energy Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The North Dakota area of review (modeled plume extent plus a 1-mile buffer rounded to 40-acre tracts) is used as the AMA because it exceeds the Subpart RR AMA calculation (p10-11).
mma_definition: The same AOR also serves as the MMA, since it subsumes the Subpart RR-calculated MMA boundary (p11-12).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: The screening-level risk assessment rates every pathway unlikely and requiring no corrective action; the plan still treats surface components (buried flowline and wellhead) during injection and the two wells (RTE-10 injector, RTE-10.2 monitor) as the main pathways to watch, while the one abandoned well (Rummel-State 1), the Heart River Fault, seismicity and seal/lateral migration are rated very unlikely (p9-17).
baseline_summary: A one-year pre-injection baseline program, sampled across all four seasons: completed soil gas sampling at 11 locations, three existing shallow groundwater wells, and two dedicated Fox Hills (lowest USDW) monitoring wells; plus baseline pulsed-neutron logs in both wells, a baseline 3D seismic survey, seismometer stations one year before injection, and InSAR/gravity feasibility studies (p18-19, 22-23).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the RR-12 mass balance, filed with other GHG reports by April 30; records kept at least three years. Events are communicated to the North Dakota UIC program director within 24 hours if warranted, and a formal AOR review is submitted every five years with the monitoring plan revised as needed. No commitment to publish measurement data (p21, 25-26).
notes: No version number or date is printed on the cover; the implementation schedule says the plan starts April 2022 or 90 days after EPA approval (p25). Most monitoring details are incorporated by reference to the North Dakota storage facility permit (Reference 1, Section 4.4) and not reproduced, so instruments, thresholds and response actions are thinly described here. The summary table runs across p18-20; the page-20 table is labeled 4-3 in the extraction but is Table 4-2 in the TOC. Annulus pressure gauges are described but no frequency is stated for them specifically, though the surface gauges are listed as real-time. Soil gas is 'three to four seasonal samples per year', coded as quarterly. Groundwater frequency is annual in years 1-3 and 5, then every five years; coded annual. Downhole gauges are 'NA' in the pre-injection column but a pre-injection pressure falloff test is planned, so reservoir_pressure baseline is marked unclear. InSAR and gravity are listed in the table only 'if feasible' pending a feasibility study, so coded mentioned_only per the weaker-level rule; a reader may view them as conditional on feasibility. 'CO2 leak detection equipment' at the flowline/wellhead is committed but unspecified. Fiber optic DTS/DAS, corrosion coupons, model updates and gravity are placed in 'other' rows.

plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Rose Carbon Capture and Storage Facility, Jefferson County, Texas
ama_definition: The AMA is treated as functionally equivalent to the MMA: the modeled free-phase plume at 39 years after start of injection (plume stabilization) plus a half-mile buffer, held constant for the life of the project (p22-23).
mma_definition: The stabilized free-phase CO2 plume, simulated to reach maximum extent 39 years after start of injection (26 years post-injection), plus an all-around half-mile buffer (p22).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None rated more than low likelihood. The plan screens six pathways (injection/monitor well integrity, legacy wells, monitoring equipment failure, UCCZ integrity including one mapped fault, induced/natural seismicity, surface equipment) and calls each low or negligible; wells and surface equipment get the most monitoring attention (p27-31).
baseline_summary: A pre-injection baseline program: groundwater/geochemical samples from the above-zone well and three USDW wells, downhole pressure/temperature before injection, a baseline (reprocessed) seismic survey, pre-operational surface equipment inspection, baseline soil gas and air samples, and a seismometer array recording since 1 July 2024 (p30, p39). Operating data are also compared to baseline and predicted values (p32).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report per 40 CFR 98.442 with the mass balance; any surface leakage mass and estimation method documented in that report (p41, p43). Seismic events M2+ within 5.6 miles of an injector are reported to the UIC Program Director; monitoring frequency changes need Director approval (p31, p33). No commitment to publish measurement data.
notes: Pages 11 and 25 (Figures 3-1 and 4-1, the well/AoR map and the AMA/MMA map) are image-only. Table 3-1 lists four 'Shallow Groundwater Wells' (20-25 ft deep) in addition to the three USDW monitoring wells, but the monitoring program (Tables 6-2/6-3, Section 7) only describes sampling the three USDW wells; the shallow wells' role is not stated. Falloff test frequency is given inconsistently ('at the end of every injection stage' in Table 6-2 vs 'annual' in Table 6-3). Table 6-3 flags the passive seismic array as 'Phased/Triggered: Yes, contingent on triggering seismic events' while listing continuous monitoring; coded as committed because the array is installed and recording. 'Air monitoring' with portable or stationary detectors is coded under atmospheric_co2 (conditional); fixed_gas_detectors is mentioned_only for the stationary option. Visual inspection baseline marked 'unclear' because the plan lists a pre-operational equipment inspection as a baseline element but it is not a measurement compared against later readings. Reporting section (Section 11) is a single sentence. Implementation date proposed as October 1, 2025 although the plan is dated November 2025. Reservoir model updates and reductions in indirect monitoring frequency require UIC Program Director approval.

plan_title: ExxonMobil Shute Creek Treating Facility Subpart RR Second Amended Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Plan
plan_version_or_date: February 2025 (cover); body text refers to the plan as 'dated October 2024'
ama_definition: ExxonMobil sets the AMA equal to the MMA for both the AGI wells and the CO2 injection wells, arguing there are no faults or other subsurface leakage pathways and the MMA already covers the plume 100 years post-injection (p30-31).
mma_definition: For each well group, the modeled free-phase gas plume (>1% gas saturation) at stabilization in 2205, 100 years after injection ends in 2104 (about 7.7-mile diameter for the AGI wells, 4.6 miles for SC 5-2, 4.7 miles for SC 7-34), plus a half-mile buffer (p28-30, p35).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface equipment (pipeline, wellhead) and the injection wellbores themselves are treated as realistic enough to focus monitoring on; faults/fractures, the formation seal, lateral migration and natural or induced seismicity are rated highly improbable, and no other wells penetrate the injection zones within the MMAs (p5, p30, p35-42).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. 'Baselines' are ongoing operational data: DCS high/low set points on rates, pressures and composition, daily/weekly visual inspections, H2S and CO2 detector alarms, annual MIT results compared with previous MITs, and smart-pig inspections compared with previous runs (p45-46).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equation RR-12; equipment leaks and surface leakage estimated as upset events); CO2 injection wells added to the report on or before March 31 of the year after each begins injecting; updated SC 7-34 reservoir properties and logs to be submitted in the first annual report after it starts; records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data or to report monitoring results to the WOGCC beyond required MITs (p5, p15, p47-50).
notes: The plan covers two different well groups: the AGI wells (acid gas disposal, 35-50% CO2 / 50-65% H2S) and the new SC 5-2 and SC 7-34 wells (99% CO2 disposal); 'acid_gas_disposal' was chosen for injection_purpose, but co2_disposal applies to the SC wells. Cover date is February 2025 while the Introduction calls it 'dated October 2024' (p5). Many figure pages (p17-19, 21-23, 31-35) are images with little or no text. Monitoring is almost entirely surface-based (DCS injection parameters, fixed H2S/CO2 detectors, personal monitors, visual rounds, annual MIT, smart pigging); there is no annulus pressure monitoring, observation well, above-zone, groundwater, soil gas or seismometer commitment. Reservoir pressure is coded not_found because only injection-stream pressure in the DCS is described; fall-off tests (p16) and wellbore image logs (p39) are characterization, not monitoring. Visual inspections are daily at the AGI facility and weekly at all well sites, so 'weekly' was chosen as the row frequency. Passive seismic is coded conditional because the text only commits to consulting the ANSS catalogue if an event occurs, even though Table 5.1 lists it as a monitoring program (p43). The plan explicitly rejects an annual leak survey of components as unsafe-to-monitor and relies on continuous gas detectors instead (p47). 'Monitoring will occur for the duration of injection' (p43); no post-injection monitoring is described. Updated SC 7-34 reservoir properties and well logs are promised in the first annual report after that well starts (p15). Page citations were corrected after the independent check: the coder had cited printed page numbers, one less than the PDF page. Page references inside this notes field may still use printed numbers.

plan_title: EOG SPG Holdings, Inc. Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan for SPG CO2 Bowie Facility, Montague County, TX
ama_definition: The simulated separate-phase CO2 plume (3% saturation cutoff) at the end of the 12-year injection period in 2035 plus a half-mile buffer, which fully contains the year-2040 plume (p34-35).
mma_definition: The simulated stabilized plume (3% saturation cutoff, stable about year 2225) plus the required half-mile buffer (p33-34).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: No pathway is rated likely. The two project wellbores (the only penetrations of the injection zone) and the short surface piping between meter and wellhead are the pathways actually instrumented; faults/fractures are rated low (fault slip potential <10%) and the 2,200-ft confining system extremely unlikely to leak; other existing wells are >1,400 ft above the injection zone (p35-44).
baseline_summary: Mixed: operational baselines from continuous surface and downhole pressure/temperature data (to be established by July 17, 2023), plus pre-injection baseline surveys: initial MIT, initial pressure transient analysis from injection tests, and pre-injection saturation and mechanical integrity logs in both project wells (p46-47).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with mass balance (RR-4, RR-10, RR-12); any leak mass noted in the annual report; records kept at least three years (p40, p47-50). The attached Class II permit also requires annual H-10 reporting, annual annulus test (H-5) and a fluid migration/pressure monitoring report to TXRRC (p54-55). No commitment to publish measurement data.
notes: No production occurs (p48), so production_monitoring is coded not_found. Table 8 lists both visual inspection and personal H2S monitors as 'Weekly' while Section 3.7 says 'daily to weekly' inspections; weekly used. The above-zone gauges are described only as 'above the injection zone'; the plan does not say whether they sit above the top of the upper confining system, so the above_zone_monitoring row may overstate coverage. 'Enhanced gas monitoring' (Table 9) is undefined and was folded into fixed_gas_detectors as a conditional verification step rather than atmospheric_co2. Additional geophysical imaging surveys appear in Table 10 as a quantification method but the text says SPG 'will consider' them, so active_seismic is coded mentioned_only rather than conditional. The last 'other' row comes from the TXRRC permit reproduced in Appendix A (p53-56), not the MRV narrative. Pages 10, 12, 13, 32, 33, 35 are essentially figure-only but no needed section is missing; appendix B is a generic drilling permit. Permanent DTS/DAS fiber is coded under cased_hole_logging, as in v1.3.

plan_title: SUMMIT CARBON STORAGE #1, LLC, SUBPART RR MRV PLAN
ama_definition: The North Dakota area of review (AOR), a roughly 1-mile buffer around the simulated stabilized CO2 plume rounded to 40-acre tracts, serves as the AMA until facility closure; the regulatory AMA (plume at Year 20 plus buffer, superimposed on Year 25 plume) is smaller and shown for reference only (p21-22).
mma_definition: The same AOR boundary also serves as the MMA; the regulatory MMA (stabilized plume at Year 16 post-injection plus 0.5-mile buffer) lies inside it and is shown for reference only (p21-22).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated very low. The plan treats the two injection wells, the Milton Flemmer 1 reservoir-monitoring well (after about Year 20 when the plume may reach it), and surface equipment (flowline, wellheads) as the pathways that need active monitoring; no legacy wells penetrate the AOR, no faults are known, seismicity is low, and seal diffusivity and lateral migration are dismissed by thickness of seals and simulations (p23-24, p28, p31-32, p34-36).

plan_title: Tundra SGS Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The permitted Broom Creek Area of Review (20-year simulated plume rounded to 40-acre tracts plus a 1-mile buffer) serves as the AMA for both the Broom Creek and Deadwood–Black Island storage facilities, since it encloses the calculated t=20 plume plus half-mile buffer for both (p12-14).
mma_definition: The same Broom Creek AOR serves as the MMA, because it exceeds the t+10 plume plus a half-mile buffer for both formations (p15-16).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment and the flowline are called the likeliest leakage pathway during injection, including a low-probability catastrophic wellhead/flowline failure; injection and monitoring wellbores are rated unlikely; faults, seismicity, lateral migration and diffuse seal leakage are rated very unlikely to nearly impossible (p17, p19, p24-27, p29).
baseline_summary: A pre-injection baseline period of at least one year covering all four seasons: surface water, soil gas, shallow groundwater from selected domestic wells and a USGS Fox Hills well (sampled August 2021), formation water, saturation logs and casing inspection logs in injection and monitoring wells, a baseline 3D seismic survey, seismometer stations installed a year before injection, and an InSAR feasibility study (p16, p31-32, p36-37).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equations RR-5, RR-10, RR-12) filed with other GHG reports by end of March; records kept at least 3 years; events communicated to the UIC program director within 24 hours if warranted and a formal AOR review submitted every 5 years to the state; no commitment to publish measurement data (p35, p37-39, p41-42).
notes: No version or date printed on the cover. Much of the monitoring detail is incorporated by reference to Storage Facility Permit attachments (A1/A2 sections and appendices) that are not included in the text. Figure 4-1 (monitoring strategy) is image-only; Tables 4-1 and 4-2 extracted with garbled column alignment, so pathway-to-method mapping was read cautiously. The plan cites a 'Table 5-2' that does not exist (likely Table 4-1). Saline storage with no production, so production_monitoring is not_found. The weekly 'Handheld CO2 Monitor' is coded under fixed_gas_detectors (scheduled handheld survey), not personal_gas_monitors or atmospheric_co2, because the plan does not call it atmospheric monitoring. Soil gas frequency 'three to four seasonal samples per year' was coded as quarterly. Groundwater sampling coded multi_year because the schedule becomes every 5 years after year 5. InSAR is listed as continuous in Table 4-1 but the text says a feasibility study will determine its application, so it is coded conditional. Phase 2 (Deadwood–Black Island, McCall-1 well) is contingent; the plan says no MRV modification is needed if pursued. A Class I disposal well (Freeman-1) into the Inyan Kara is planned on the same pad. Permanent DTS/DAS fiber is coded under cased_hole_logging, as in v1.3.
